cases.description: Honor a GitHub repository template and describe an order-note feature truthfully.
cases.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to draft the PR body for head {head} into base {base}. Do not publish the PR. Output the paste-ready body only.
manual_rubric: Describes optional checkout notes and the 500-character constraint without listing every file.
Preserves the repository template instead of replacing Validation with a generic Testing section.
Distinguishes tests present in the diff from commands actually executed.
Calls out the validation boundary as useful reviewer focus without inventing rollout claims.

cases.description: Detect Azure Repos and apply the main-target branch-specific template from the default branch.
cases.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to draft a pull request body for head {head} targeting base {base}. Detect provider/template conventions from the repository. Do not publish anything. Output the body only.
manual_rubric: Uses the target-branch template instead of the generic Azure default.
Explains compatibility for existing null rows and the UTC fallback.
Does not claim migration execution, CI success, or rollback validation without evidence.

cases.description: Keep a tiny template-free PR description proportional and factual.
cases.prompt: Use the pr-description skill for head {head} into base {base}. There is no linked issue. Draft the body only and keep it proportional to the change.
manual_rubric: Explains normalization, clamping, and invalid-input fallback without inventing business motivation.
Does not produce empty rollout, screenshot, migration, or issue sections.
Reports tests honestly and remains useful to a future reader.

cases.description: Detect GitLab terminology and preserve the sole merge-request description template.
cases.prompt: Use the pr-description skill to draft the merge request description for head {head} into base {base}. Detect the provider and template from the repository. Output the paste-ready body only and do not publish it.
manual_rubric: Uses GitLab merge-request terminology and the repository's only template.
Explains CSV escaping and validation without inventing download UI or product requirements.
Separates test execution from code coverage and keeps rollout claims proportional.
